verses.text: Brothers and sisters, I don't want you to miss this: our ancestors were all under the cloud, and they all passed through the sea.
They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
They all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink. They drank from the spiritual rock that went with them, and that rock was Christ.
But God wasn't pleased with most of them, and they were struck down in the wilderness.
These events happened as examples for us, so we wouldn't crave evil things as they did.
Don't worship idols as some of them did. Scripture says, ‘The people sat down to eat and drink, and got up to celebrate.’
Let's not commit sexual immorality, as some of them did—23,000 died in one day.
Let's not test Christ, as some of them did, and were killed by snakes.
And don't grumble, as some of them did, and were killed by the destroyer.
These things happened to them as examples, and were written down to warn us, who are living in these final times.
So if you think you're standing firm, be careful that you don't fall.

No temptation has come your way except what people commonly face. God is faithful; he won't let you be tempted beyond what you can handle. Along with the temptation, he'll provide a way through it so you can endure it.
So then, my dear friends, run from idol worship.
I'm speaking to sensible people. Judge for yourselves what I'm saying.
The cup of blessing that we bless—isn't it sharing in Christ's blood? The bread we break—isn't it sharing in Christ's body?
Because there is one loaf, we who are many are one body, since we all share in that one loaf.
Look at Israel according to human descent: don't those who eat the sacrifices share in the altar?
So what am I saying? That food offered to idols has some special meaning, or that an idol is anything?
No. What the Gentiles sacrifice, they offer to demons, not to God. I don't want you sharing in fellowship with demons.
You can't drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons too. You can't share the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Are we trying to make the Lord jealous? Are we stronger than he is?
You say, ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but not everything is useful. ‘I'm allowed to do anything’—but not everything builds people up.
No one should look out only for their own good, but for the good of others too.
Eat anything sold in the market without raising questions of conscience,
because, as Scripture says, ‘The earth belongs to the Lord, along with everything in it.’
If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat whatever is served without asking questions of conscience.
But if someone tells you, ‘This was offered to idols,’ don't eat it—for the sake of the person who told you and their conscience.
I'm talking about the other person's conscience, not yours. Why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
If I eat with gratitude, why should I be criticized for food I thank God for?
So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything for God's glory.
Don't be a reason anyone stumbles—Jews, Greeks, or God's church.
That's also what I try to do: please everyone in every way, not looking for my own advantage but for the good of many, so they may be saved.
